audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, and neither layer ever gave a number for the blind.
audit.why: Blinding Dart is 7 seconds at every rank — it does not scale down. Siphoning Strike goes 7.5/6.5/5.5/4.5/3.5s. That means the gap between his blinds is fixed while Nasus's window shrinks every rank, until late in the game Nasus gets two empowered Qs per blind. That single comparison is the whole matchup clock and it was nowhere in the data.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart 7s flat vs Siphoning Strike 7.5s falling to 3.5s. Bait the blind on a junk auto, then commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Move Quick is never named and its actual weakness is never stated. Both layers just say Teemo 'kites on move speed'.
audit.why: Riot's text: the passive move speed lasts until he is struck by an enemy champion or turret. It is not a permanent steroid — one connecting hit takes it off him. That reframes the approach from 'I cannot catch him' to 'land anything, then close'.
audit.corrected: Move Quick's passive speed ends the moment an enemy champion strikes him.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer chart gave Teemo all five stages through level 6 at 7-8/10; the content chart gives him only stages 1 and 4, with Nasus on stages 5 and 6.
audit.why: Nasus wins 51.1% over 773 games. The two charts on the same page disagreed about who wins at level 6 and at first item, which is exactly the decision a loading-screen coach exists to make.
audit.corrected: phases[1] and [2] moved to Skill, phases[4] and [5] to Nasus, matching the content chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged "Use Spirit Fire" in wants.you[1] as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: False positive — Spirit Fire is Nasus's E. The checker matched the leading verb into the name.

audit.whatIsWrong: Checked whether the level-6 spike claim holds up.
audit.why: Teemo has no dash and no blink in his kit; the only mobility is Move Quick, which Wither directly answers and which a single strike removes. The existing claim that level 6 plus Wither is the one window he cannot escape is sound, so I sharpened the wording rather than changing the call.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json — full ability list, no dash flag

edits.after: Move Quick's passive speed ends the moment an enemy champion strikes him — chip him first, then try to close.

edits.before: E lets you stack safely from range when Teemo zones you. Spirit Fire the wave under tower; every stack denied is his only real win condition.
edits.after: Wither is online but hold it: Blinding Dart is 7s flat at every rank, so eat it on a throwaway auto first, then Wither and walk him down.

edits.after: Fury of the Sands plus Wither is the one window he cannot kite — pop R, slow him, and he has no dash and no blink to leave.

edits.after: - Teemo Blinding Dart: 7s flat at every rank — bait it on a junk auto, then Wither and run him down in that window.

edits.before: Negates your autos. Wither him after. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Blinds your autos and it is 7s flat at every rank — bait it, then commit.

edits.before: Teemo wastes Blinding Dart — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Blinding Dart stays 7s at all ranks while your Q falls to 3.5s.

edits.after: Noxious Trap slows you in place while his poison and his poke tick.

edits.before: Fury of the Sands plus Wither finally lets me catch him: ult the gap, point-click W to gut his move speed, and run him down before his blind comes back.
edits.after: Wait for Blinding Dart to be spent before I ult in: it is 7s flat, so blow the blind on a junk auto, then R, Wither his move speed, and run him down.

notes: Left the Noxious Trap 'knockup' flag in champ-data/_kits/teemo.json alone and did not write anything based on it — mushrooms slow, they do not displace, so that derived flag looks like a false positive from the flag builder.
